title: The 5 PM Slide Deck Disaster
theme: Leo's presentation day (everything that can sabotage a talk, from 7 AM alarm to the 5 PM stage)
premise: Leo needs to deliver a ten-minute presentation at 5 PM to keep his job, but his brain treats a minor slide deck as a life-or-death battle for survival. Mia agrees to drag him to the finish line, mostly to see if he will physically melt from stress.
running_gag: a squeaking neon-green dolphin laser pointer that Leo bought for luck and keeps accidentally triggering at terrible moments
payoff: When Leo panics on stage, he accidentally targets his boss's chin with the squeaking dolphin laser, turning his paralyzing fear into an absurd icebreaker that wins over the room.
description: Leo has 10 minutes to pitch his slides, but his overactive brain is convinced every minor mistake will trigger social ruin. Watch Mia try to keep him grounded using blunt roasts, cold brew, and an absurdly loud dolphin laser pointer. Can a little psychological understanding help Leo survive the scariest 5 PM of his life?

scenes.setting: Leo's tiny apartment kitchen, cluttered with 12 half-empty coffee mugs, cue cards taped to the microwave, and a grumpy landlord in a floral bathrobe peering through the window.
scenes.beat: Leo rehearses slide one 40 times while clutching his neon-green dolphin laser pointer, convinced a single typo will end in immediate homelessness. Mia drinks cold brew straight from his carton, noting that if he dies of stress today, she is taking his good pillows.

story.title: The 5 PM Slide Deck Disaster
story.insight: Treating a minor setback as a total catastrophe creates extra stress.
story.caption: Why does one typo feel like a total career collapse?

shots.scene: Leo holds a neon-green dolphin laser pointer in a cramped kitchen. A neighbor in a floral robe watches from the window.

lines.text: If this font is wrong, I will surely be homeless by sunset.

shots.scene: Leo paces near a stack of twelve coffee mugs while Mia leans against the microwave, drinking from a milk carton.

lines.text: Your landlord is watching you sweat, and it is honestly quite impressive.
He knows I am a failure who cannot align a simple text box!

shots.scene: The laser pointer accidentally clicks, casting a neon dot on the neighbor's forehead. Leo shakes violently.

lines.text: You just targeted a man in a bathrobe with a plastic dolphin.
That is it, I am officially a criminal and my life is over.

shots.scene: Mia sets the carton down, looking at Leo with a flat, bored expression.

lines.text: You are catastrophizing, taking one tiny error and inflating it into a disaster.

shots.scene: Leo stares at the ceiling. Mia checks her watch, looking unimpressed by his drama.

lines.text: Just pause for a second and ask yourself what actually happens if you fail.

shots.scene: Leo looks at the neon-green dolphin, his hand trembling slightly.

lines.text: But if I don't prepare for the absolute worst case,

scenes.setting: A cramped coffee shop where a barista with a handlebar mustache and a stained apron glares from behind a sputtering espresso machine.
scenes.beat: Leo spills exactly three drops of oat milk on his yellow hoodie and assumes every person in the cafe is mentally documenting his complete downfall. Mia tests the squeaking dolphin laser on a stranger's tote bag to prove nobody is paying attention to his tiny stain.

story.title: The 5 PM Slide Deck Disaster
story.insight: We think everyone stares at our tiny flaws, but they barely notice.
story.caption: Three drops of oat milk and Leo thinks his life is over.

shots.scene: Cramped coffee shop at 1:30 PM. A glaring barista with a handlebar mustache works an espresso machine. Leo stares at his yellow hoodie, panicking, while clutching a neon-green dolphin laser pointer. Mia sips cold brew.

lines.text: Everyone in this cafe just watched me ruin my life.
It is three drops of oat milk, not an execution.

shots.scene: Same coffee shop. Leo frantically dabbing his yellow hoodie with a tiny napkin. Mia points the squeaking green dolphin laser at a stranger's canvas tote bag.

lines.text: That hipster with the mustache is memorizing my exact failure.
He is literally staring at foam, Leo, not your tragedy.

shots.scene: Coffee shop counter. Leo sweating through his yellow hoodie, accidentally clicking the dolphin laser. Mia casually steals a pastry from his tray.

lines.text: My entire professional legacy is currently dissolving into cotton fibers.
Your legacy is a stained hoodie and bad posture.

shots.scene: Coffee shop table. Mia holds up her phone to block Leo's view of the crowd. Leo blinks in sudden confusion.

lines.text: You are experiencing the spotlight effect right now.
The what effect?

shots.scene: Coffee shop corner. Mia pats Leo's shoulder with exaggerated pity. Leo clutches his neon-green dolphin laser like a lifeline.

lines.text: Assume nobody cares, because frankly, they really do not.

shots.scene: Coffee shop exit. Leo zips his yellow hoodie all the way up to his nose. Mia rolls her eyes and pushes the door open.

lines.text: Everyone in this cafe just watched me ruin my life.

scenes.setting: The fluorescent-lit office holding room, filled with stale donut boxes and a rival presenter in a tight grey suit hyperventilating into a paper bag.
scenes.beat: Leo insists he was accidentally hired three years ago and tries to hide under a plastic folding table. Mia gives him a savage pep talk, reminding him that his coworkers are far too lazy to notice he is faking it, while repeatedly squeaking the dolphin laser near his ear.

story.title: The 5 PM Slide Deck Disaster
story.insight: Feeling like a fraud just means you care.
story.caption: Leo tries to hide under a folding table at 4:15 PM.

shots.scene: Bright office holding room with stale donuts, a rival in a tight grey suit hyperventilating in the background. Leo and Mia facing camera, Leo trying to crawl under a plastic table.

lines.text: I was accidentally hired three years ago and now they will know.
Stop whimpering under the folding table, you are thirty-one.

shots.scene: Holding room with a half-eaten donut box on a desk, rival still breathing into a paper bag. Leo clutching a squeaking neon-green dolphin laser pointer.

lines.text: My slides use basic shapes, they are going to deport me.
No one cares about your triangles, Leo, they want free pizza.

shots.scene: Holding room with fluorescent lights buzzing, rival nervously adjusting his grey tie. Mia aggressively squeaking the green dolphin pointer near Leo's ear.

lines.text: The dolphin laser is squeaking because my career is dying.
It squeaks because you are pressing the button with your thumb.

shots.scene: Holding room with a stack of paper plates on the counter, rival staring blankly at the wall. Mia tapping her teal sweater sleeve.

lines.text: This is classic imposter syndrome, where competent people feel like total frauds.
You mean I am not an accidental employee on trial?

shots.scene: Holding room with empty coffee cups scattered everywhere, rival finally lowering his paper bag. Mia handing Leo a warm paper cup.

lines.text: Should I just focus on my third slide instead?
Drink this cold brew and pretend you belong here.

shots.scene: Holding room with the rival packing his bag, door marked conference room ahead. Leo holding his neon dolphin pointer tightly.

lines.text: What if the projector screen actually catches fire right now?

scenes.setting: The packed auditorium stage, with Leo's terrifying boss—a woman in a sharp red blazer—staring sternly from the front row.
scenes.beat: When Leo forces himself to stand tall and hold out his hands, the confident posture can trick his brain into feeling calm, even as he accidentally shines the squeaking dolphin laser right on his boss's chin. The entire room bursts into laughter, and Leo effortlessly glides through his slides.

story.title: The 5 PM Slide Deck Disaster
story.insight: Physical posture can trick your nervous system into feeling safe.
story.caption: How a fake power pose saves a career at five PM.

shots.scene: Stage edges, Leo in yellow hoodie holding squeaking neon dolphin laser pointer, Mia in teal sweater beside him, red-blazer boss staring from front row.

lines.text: My legs have literally fused into the auditorium floorboards.
Stop whining and just stand upright like a normal human.

shots.scene: Bright stage lights, Leo stretching arms wide, boss glaring from front row with folded arms, Mia smirking.

lines.text: I am radiating confidence while my soul attempts to exit.
Your ribs are practically touching your spine right now.

shots.scene: Stage podium, Leo striking a wide power pose, accidentally clicking the neon dolphin laser pointer onto boss's chin.

lines.text: Wait, why is the dolphin squeaking at her chin?
You just illuminated her face with a glowing green mammal.

shots.scene: Auditorium filled with blurry laughing coworkers, boss smirking, Leo standing tall, Mia looking impressed.

lines.text: That is embodied cognition, where physical poses actually calm brains.
The laughter magically stopped my entire nervous system from melting.

shots.scene: Center stage podium, Leo gesturing smoothly at blank screen, boss nodding approvingly, Mia leaning against backdrop.

lines.text: Watch me seamlessly glide through these ridiculous corporate slides.
Try not to faint until slide four at least.

shots.scene: Auditorium stage, Leo holding pointer high, boss watching intently, Mia giving thumbs up.

lines.text: My legs have literally fused into the auditorium floorboards.

title: The Moving Day Trap
theme: Leo moves into a new apartment (decisions, boxes, neighbours, first night)
premise: Leo wants to perfectly setup his new apartment before midnight to prove he finally has his life together. What's at stake is his sanity when he realizes he has unpacked only one houseplant and forty-two mismatched socks.
running_gag: Gerald the houseplant being treated like a fragile royal heir while actual furniture gets destroyed.
payoff: Leo sleeps on a bare floor wrapped in bubble wrap, but Gerald the plant gets the only assembled bed under a dedicated spotlight.
description: Moving into a new place is supposed to mean a fresh start, but Leo turns unpacking into an extreme mental sport. Watch Mia track his questionable choices while Gerald the houseplant receives five-star accommodations. Will Leo survive his first night without overthinking the wallpaper?

scenes.setting: Leo's new living room, wall-to-wall cardboard boxes
scenes.beat: Leo spends forty-seven minutes agonizing over whether to unpack the coffee mugs or the spatula first while Mia eats cold pizza on a box labelled 'IMPORTANT/DO NOT TOUCH'. Mia quotes Kyle's text ('Kyle says: just throw everything in one pile and light a scented candle, bro') and updates her Told-You-So Scoreboard to 24 after Leo accidentally tapes Gerald the plant inside a moving crate.

story.title: The Moving Day Trap
story.insight: Endless tiny choices drain your brain's decision power fast.
story.caption: Why does moving make simple choices feel impossible? Meet decision fatigue.

shots.scene: Leo stands in a box-filled living room holding a spatula with worried eyes. Mia sits on a box marked IMPORTANT eating pizza with a smirk.

lines.text: This spatula decides if I'm responsible or a dumpster raccoon!
You spent forty minutes weeping over three ceramic mugs.

shots.scene: Leo gestures anxiously near forty-two mismatched socks. Mia checks her phone flatly. Outside the window, Dev the barista passes carrying Leeo's coffee.

lines.text: Okay but hear me out, mugs demand deep emotional balance!
Kyle texted: burn the socks and claim insurance, bro.

shots.scene: Leo stands frozen next to a crate labelled GERALD, looking sheepish. Mia writes twenty-four on a tiny notepad with raised eyebrows.

lines.text: I accidentally taped Gerald the plant into crate seven!
Scoreboard update: twenty-four for me, zero for Leo.

shots.scene: Leo slumps tiredly against a stack of boxes. Mia steps closer, facing front with a calm, analytical expression.

lines.text: Decision fatigue struck—too many tiny choices fried your brain.
This is the Sunday Blanket Panic with bubble wrap!

shots.scene: Leo looks at a silver coin with hopeful eyes. Mia points at the boxes with a sly smirk, calm and upright.

lines.text: Flip a coin for small choices. Next time: sofa staircase trap.

shots.scene: Mia stands directly beside crate seven, staring at the packaging tape with a deadpan closed-mouth expression.

lines.text: Anyway. You trapped an innocent houseplant in total darkness.

scenes.setting: Apartment hallway, outside neighbour Brenda's open door
scenes.beat: Leo drops a squeaky rubber chicken while carrying Gerald, convincing himself that nosy neighbour Brenda—visible in her floral cardigan holding a clipboard—now considers him a menace to the building's peace. Mia dryly points out Brenda hasn't looked up from her Sudoku once, while Leo over-explains the acoustics of linoleum flooring to an empty corridor.

story.title: The Moving Day Trap
story.insight: People notice your awkward moments way less than you think.
story.caption: Dropped something in public and thought everyone was judging you? That's the Spotlight Effect taking over.

shots.scene: Linoleum apartment corridor with stacked boxes. Leo in yellow hoodie gently cradles potted fern Gerald. Mia in teal sweater stands beside him with raised eyebrows. Neighbour Brenda visible behind.

lines.text: The entire building officially hates me now.
I dropped Gerald's emotional support squeaky-chicken near Brenda's door.

shots.scene: Leo crouches near linoleum floor with worried eyes, pointing dramatically at squeaky chicken toy. Mia stands upright with smirk, holding clipboard. Neighbour Brenda sits quietly in background.

lines.text: Brenda is seventy-two and solving a hard Sudoku.
She wrote 'loud menace' on her clipboard, Mia!

shots.scene: Leo hugs Gerald the plant closer with panicked eyes. Mia looks down at her phone with deadpan expression. Brenda remains seated near her apartment doorway in background.

lines.text: Linoleum amplifies squeaks! Remember the Sunday Blanket Panic?
Kyle texts: tell Brenda you're testing acoustics for your opera career.

shots.scene: Mia stands with folded arms, deadpan gaze facing camera. Leo stands beside her looking sheepish. Brenda in background flips a puzzle page, unaware of them. In the background, clearly visible and drawn in the same style, stands a curious stranger watching from a bench (the person being talked about), smaller than Leo and Mia and at the edge of the frame, never blocking their faces.

lines.text: It's the SPOTLIGHT EFFECT.
We overestimate how much strangers notice our tiny, awkward mistakes.

shots.scene: Leo gently rests Gerald on a cardboard box with relieved expression. Mia stands beside him with warm smirk, arms loosely crossed. Brenda visible near background door.

lines.text: Try assuming nobody cares, because honestly, nobody does.

shots.scene: Mia leans against the apartment corridor wall, looking at Leo with amused, raised eyebrow. Leo stands facing camera with anxious eyes. Brenda remains quiet in background.

lines.text: Why do you always insist that...

scenes.setting: Kitchen counter strewn with takeaway containers
scenes.beat: Leo refuses to abandon a wobbly, three-legged stool he spent four hours assembling backwards because 'it represents my transition into adult self-reliance.' Mia reminds him this is worse than his breakdown during The Sunday Blanket Panic, while Dev the barista passes in the alley outside delivering coffee mislabeled 'Leon'.

story.title: The Moving Day Trap
story.insight: We cling to bad choices just because we suffered to make them.
story.caption: Spending four hours building a stool backwards doesn't make it art, Leo.

shots.scene: A cramped kitchen counter at 7:10 PM with greasy takeaway boxes. Leo hugs a fragile, overly dressed Gerald the plant while staring at a wobbly three-legged stool. In the blurry alley window behind them, Dev the barista walks past holding a cup labeled 'Leon'.

lines.text: This backward stool is my absolute crowning achievement in adult self-reliance!
It has three legs and actively hunts my ankles.

shots.scene: Leo aggressively tightens a loose wooden screw on the deformed stool with a butter knife. Gerald the plant wears a tiny paper crown on its single healthy leaf. Mia checks her phone with a bored tilt of her head.

lines.text: Okay but hear me out. I bled twice on the cushion.
That is sadder than your breakdown during The Sunday Blanket Panic.

shots.scene: Leo raises the lopsided stool above his head like a triumphant trophy hunter. Mia pinches the bridge of her nose in deep regret, her teal sweater sleeves bunched up.

lines.text: If I quit now, those four hours of pure agony were completely free!

shots.scene: Leo lowers the stool gently. Mia points a single fake-nail finger straight at his chest, leaning in close with absolute deadpan confidence.

lines.text: That is the sunk cost fallacy. You are proposing to garbage.

shots.scene: Leo sets Gerald the plant onto the wobbly seat. The stool immediately collapses into a pile of sad matchsticks. Leo stares blankly down at the wreckage.

lines.text: Next time, I am hiring a professional toddler to build furniture.

shots.scene: Leo gingerly scoops Gerald the plant out of the sawdust pile, cradling it like a fragile royal heir while the broken stool parts roll across the floor.

lines.text: Are we framing the splintered wood as avant-garde wall decor?

scenes.setting: Unfurnished bedroom with one solitary lamp
scenes.beat: Faced with eighty-four white noise tracks to help him sleep in the new room, Leo overthinks until 1:00 AM while Mia leaves him sleeping on a bubble-wrap mattress next to a perfectly cushioned Gerald. Next time: Leo tries to host his first adult dinner party and accidentally invites his boss Greg.

story.title: The Moving Day Trap
story.caption: When choosing a white noise track ruins your entire night.

shots.scene: Unfurnished bedroom at 11:05 PM with one lamp. Leo sits cross-legged on bubble wrap next to Gerald the plant on a velvet cushion. Mia leans against the bare wall eating cold pizza.

lines.text: Eighty-four white noise tracks remain.
Pick rain, Leo. It's midnight.

shots.scene: Leo scrolls frantically on his phone. Gerald wears a tiny velvet eye mask propped on a toothpick. A lonely lamp casts harsh shadows.

lines.text: But what if brown noise heals me faster than pink rain?
You are vibrating at a frequency of pure regret.

shots.scene: Leo holds his phone inches from his face, sweating under the harsh lamp. Gerald looks suspiciously serene on the cushion.

lines.text: The thunderstorm track has aggressive thunderclaps!
That is worse than your Sunday Blanket Panic.

shots.scene: Mia points at Leo's phone as he stares blankly. Gerald's eye mask slips slightly. The apartment is dead silent.

lines.text: This is the paradox of choice, Leo.
Extra options guarantee zero decisions.

shots.scene: Mia walks out the door, leaving Leo slumped against the bubble wrap. Gerald rests on the luxury cushion with the only pillow.

lines.text: Just flip a coin.

shots.scene: Leo fast asleep upright against the wall, mouth open. Gerald sits comfortably on the plush cushion next to him. Lamp hums.

lines.text: Next time: Greg gets invited.
